official_wagers.reason: Established UFC samples on both sides (11 vs 5 prior UFC bouts), reference and v0.33 agree on Boser, very large price edge, and no sparse-data block. Method remains non-official because winner probability is below the method promotion floor.

Buckley winner probability clears the winner floor; KO is the top method in baseline, calibrated and residual layers; calibrated conditional KO probability is 0.7338195935 and exact calibrated joint KO probability is 0.4595376409; no sparse-data block. Chosen over Buckley ML under the one-wager-per-fight rule because the exact method clears governance and offers stronger modeled value.

passes_and_watchlist.note: Chovancek ML -134 has only about a 1.5 percentage-point edge and Chovancek is a UFC debutant.

Croden ML is materially overpriced versus the frozen 53.8% Stage A probability. Chandler +270 is reverse-side value from a near-coinflip model, but price alone is not enough to flip the frozen side and research did not establish a material omitted fact.
Koslow ML -166 shows a positive model edge, but Koslow has one prior UFC bout and a 1407-day layoff; sparse and inactivity risk prevent an official wager.
Stage A strongly favors Stiller while FanDuel strongly favors Cerminara. Stiller is making her UFC debut against a highly experienced former title challenger; the disagreement is tracked, not bet.
Mahjoub +112 has a modest positive edge, but both fighters are UFC debutants.

Leblanc +480 creates an extreme raw edge in the frozen model, but the matchup is one UFC bout versus a debutant and current research materially supports caution: Leblanc was stopped in his UFC debut while Galanti enters 8-1 after a 35-second DWCS knockout and a regional title run. No official wager.
Landwehr +235 is large raw value, but Stage A is only a 52.9% lean, Nallo has one UFC bout, Landwehr is 38, moving to lightweight and enters after three straight stoppage losses. No official wager.
Jourdain ML -166 is more expensive than the frozen 58.5% probability and Jourdain is a UFC debutant.

Daukaus ML -200 has only a thin edge. KO/TKO-or-points +125 is positive by the calibrated union, but method layers disagree and submission remains a meaningful Daukaus path, so the derivative is not promoted.
Perez ML -340 is overpriced. Nelson +275 is reverse-side value, but Perez is a UFC debutant with strong regional/DWCS finishing credentials and the frozen Stage A side remains Perez.
Blanchfield is one of the stronger Stage A sides, but -330 is more expensive than the frozen 73.0% win probability and the method/timing derivatives are also priced beyond model value.

timing_review.note: No timing market cleared the full combination of edge threshold, research-coherence and sparse-data rules. Boser-Diniz GTD YES had a numerical edge but conflicted with finish-risk evidence; several larger timing discrepancies occurred in sparse/debutant fights and remain blocked.
